renderInstructions.description: Render as a responsive course catalogue and module learning experience.
renderInstructions.navigation: Show domain cards first, then module cards in sequence order.
uiRules: Use arrays as repeatable cards or lists.
Keep source URLs as clickable links.
Show assessment and completion items in a distinct panel.
Do not display internal source_content or checksum fields as learner-facing text.
renderInstructions.brandingRule: Use branding.logo.dataUri as the primary image source; if data URIs are not supported, use branding.logo.fileName after uploading 92954.png as a companion asset.
renderInstructions.certificateRule: Render the certificate using certificateDesign. Use the embedded institutional logo as the visible seal and a low-opacity watermark. Keep certificate fields dynamic and never hard-code a learner name, date or certificate ID.
renderInstructions.checkpointQuizRule: After each tenth module in a domain, render the corresponding five-question checkpoint quiz before continuing to the next domain.
renderInstructions.dataSafety: Keep answerKey, explanation and rubric fields server-side or teacher-only in production. Learner mode must receive the randomized attempt payload, not the complete answer bank.
renderInstructions.singleUploadNote: The master JSON contains the embedded randomizer sourceCode; the separate .js file is supplied for direct Node.js execution.
renderInstructions.singleFileRule: This single JSON contains the complete course, quizzes, final assessment, embedded randomizer, logo, certificate design and login-profile bindings.
renderInstructions.loginCertificateRule: For a logged-in learner, bind certificate learnerName to auth.currentUser.displayName. Do not show or issue a certificate for an unauthenticated user.
renderInstructions.themeRule: Render the website in light theme only: white/light-gray surfaces, navy and blue text, restrained antique-gold accents, professional international education styling.
renderInstructions.standardsRule: Treat internationalStandards as implementation targets. Do not claim external certification unless separately audited and approved.
renderInstructions.aboutPageRule: Render aboutPage at /about without altering any D01–D04 or final-assessment content.
renderInstructions.courseCreatorRule: Render aboutPage.courseCreator as a 300–400 word professional profile with name, title, institutional affiliation and two external CTA buttons. Preserve the bio text exactly as stored.

lookupRules: Find a domain with domains[].id equal to the route domainId.
Find a module with modules[].id equal to the route moduleId.
Find a checkpoint quiz with checkpointQuizzes[].afterModuleId equal to the completed module ID.
Render only the randomized learner attempt, never finalAssessment.questionBank, for learner assessment pages.
Render certificate pages only when certificateEligibility.isEligible is true.

courseStandards.completionRule: A learner completes the D01–D04 stage when all 60 modules are completed, required knowledge checks and activities are attempted, reflections are submitted, and the four applied domain labs meet the stated rubric and evidence requirements.

learningDesign.evidence_principle: Learners must connect recommendations to facts, assumptions, stakeholders, risks, controls, evidence, uncertainty, owners and review triggers.
learningDesign.accessibility_standard: Materials and assessments should be available in accessible digital formats, use clear language, provide reasonable alternatives for activities, and avoid requiring disclosure of sensitive personal data.

formative: knowledge checks with explanations or rationales
summative: domain applied case lab for D01.15
domain applied regulatory case lab for D02.15
domain applied risk and assurance lab for D03.15
domain applied lifecycle governance lab for D04.15
assessment.academic_integrity: Learners must identify sources, distinguish law from standards and guidance, label assumptions and synthetic cases, and disclose material use of AI assistance according to Global Learning policy.

checkpointQuizPolicy.attempts: Allow provider-configured retakes; retain the highest or latest score according to Global Learning policy.
checkpointQuizPolicy.source: Questions are selected from the existing module knowledge checks; no new learner-facing subject matter was invented.

quality.maintenance: Review jurisdiction-specific and time-sensitive content before each delivery cycle and after material legal, regulatory, standards or technology changes.
quality.release_gate: No learner release until all JSON parses, module IDs are unique and complete, required fields are present, sources are traceable, assessment keys are reviewed and the provider approves the current version.

aboutPage.title: About Atlas Education
aboutPage.subtitle: Global Learning for responsible professional practice

sections.heading: Atlas Education
sections.body: Atlas Education is a Global Learning institution focused on professional, accessible and internationally oriented education. It supports learners who want to develop practical knowledge, responsible judgement and evidence-informed professional capability.

sections.heading: Our Mission
sections.body: Our mission is to make high-quality professional learning clear, structured and applicable across diverse institutional and cultural contexts.

sections.heading: Our Learning Approach
sections.body: The learning experience combines structured modules, applied activities, case analysis, reflection, knowledge checks and multi-format assessment. Learners are encouraged to connect concepts with responsible practice, evidence and real-world decision-making.

sections.heading: Global Perspective
sections.body: Global Learning uses internationally relevant examples and recognises that governance, technology, institutions and communities operate in different legal, cultural, linguistic and resource contexts.

sections.heading: Assessment Integrity
sections.body: Assessment results are designed to reflect learner achievement through varied question formats, written work, scenario responses, evidence review and authenticated learner records. The pass rule is strictly greater than 75 percent.

sections.heading: Certificate of Completion
sections.body: Eligible learners receive a professionally designed certificate after completing the required modules, checkpoint assessments, final assessment and written-review requirements. Certificate identity is bound to the authenticated learner profile.

sections.heading: Institutional Information
sections.body: For institutional, accessibility, verification or programme questions, use the approved Atlas Education contact and support channels configured by the institution.

aboutPage.disclaimer: This About page describes the learning platform and programme approach. It does not make a claim of government accreditation, regulatory approval or external certification unless separately verified and published by Atlas Education.

courseCreator.name: Nafiul Ahmad Rafi
courseCreator.title: Founding Director, Atlas AI Institute · AI Governance and Public Policy Researcher
courseCreator.institutionalAffiliation: Atlas AI Institute; National AI Policy Endorser, AI Policy Lab, Umeå University, Sweden
courseCreator.bio:
Nafiul Ahmad Rafi is an AI governance and public policy researcher, policy architect and education leader based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. He is the Founding Director of Atlas AI Institute and serves as a National AI Policy Endorser at the AI Policy Lab, Umeå University, Sweden. His work focuses on the institutional, regulatory and human capacity required for responsible AI adoption in Bangladesh, South Asia and the wider Global South.

Rafi’s research examines how countries can build practical AI governance systems that reflect local realities while participating meaningfully in international standards and multilateral policy processes. He has analysed AI governance infrastructure across 75 countries and developed research and policy frameworks addressing regulatory capacity, institutional readiness, equitable representation and responsible innovation. His work includes the Global South AI Policy Framework and a growing body of publications on AI policy, governance and technology for developing and emerging economies.

Through Atlas AI Institute, Rafi connects research with applied education, civic technology and public-interest infrastructure. The Institute’s work includes AI governance research, policy intelligence, digital inclusion initiatives and practical tools such as the Nagorik AI Assistant, FactCheckBD, Atlas OS and the Atlas AII Global AI Policy Hub. This approach reflects a commitment to AI for good: developing systems that are useful, understandable, rights-aware and relevant to communities that are often underrepresented in technology debates.

As the course creator, Rafi brings together policy research, institutional analysis, ethical reasoning and applied learning. The Atlas Education Global Learning programme is designed to build AI literacy and professional capability for the next generation of leaders, educators, researchers, public servants and practitioners. Its purpose is not only to explain AI, but to help learners evaluate its social consequences, design responsible governance responses and contribute constructively to a changing global environment.

Rafi is a policy network member of CIVICUS, a member of the Internet Society and a member of the Responsible AI Hub. His institutional work through Atlas AI Institute advances accessible AI education, Global South perspectives and the development of future-ready professionals.
